$comment: Reviewer registry for `dotf pr triage-queue` (#403).
The queue asks ONE question: is there reviewer output on an open PR that
nobody has dispositioned? Without this file the command cannot answer, and
it exits non-zero saying so — deliberately, because an unanswerable queue
must never be mistaken for a clear one. Before this file existed, every PR
in this repository closed with the Definition of Done's evidence item
skipped rather than met.
Only `coderabbitai` is registered, because it is the only reviewer that
runs here. mlorentedev/dotfiles additionally registers `github-actions`
for PR-Agent; hive has no such workflow, and declaring a reviewer that
cannot run would make this file assert a review that never happens.
WHY `review_markers` IS THE SUMMARY COMMENT AND NOT THE REVIEW ITSELF.
This is the load-bearing detail and it is not obvious. On this repository
CodeRabbit files PROPER reviews through the reviews API — measured on
#401, where a 5-finding review reads `**Actionable comments posted: 5**`
in `reviews[]`. But the queue reads `gh pr list --json comments`, which
returns issue comments ONLY and never `reviews[]`. So the review itself is
invisible to this consumer, and matching on its text would leave the queue
permanently empty on a repository that is being reviewed — the exact false
clear this file exists to prevent.
The marker below is the walkthrough comment CodeRabbit posts alongside
every review, which IS comment-shaped. Verified present on both PRs open
at the time of writing: #401 (a real review) and #406 (a decline).
KNOWN LIMITATION, stated rather than discovered later: the walkthrough is
posted once per PR and EDITED on re-review, and `createdAt` does not move
on an edit. So a second review after a push may not re-open the queue for
a PR already triaged once. The queue is therefore a floor, not a ceiling.
Closing that gap needs a consumer that reads `reviews[]`, which is a
change to the dotfiles CLI and not to this file.
`declined_markers` identify CodeRabbit's 'I could not review' notice.
Matched as the machine-emitted HTML marker rather than the prose, because
prose is reworded and the marker is not.
`advisory: true` — same disposition as dotfiles, and independently
measured here: on #406 (2026-08-25) CodeRabbit was rate limited, posted
'Review limit reached', and its COMMIT STATUS READ `success`. A green
check that means no review ran is the failure this whole mechanism exists
to catch. Advisory means its decline does not refuse the change — a quota
is a billing state of a third party, not a property of the diff — while
its review still attests.
Note what follows from the two settings together, and is intended: the
decline notice ALSO carries the walkthrough marker, so a rate-limited PR
reads as reviewer output awaiting disposition rather than as a clear
queue. That is the honest answer. A notice that no review ran leaves the
PR unreviewed, and proceeding on it is allowed — proceeding silently is
not.
Deliberately ABSENT: the `escape` and `exempt` blocks dotfiles carries.
Those are read by its review-attestation CI gate, which hive does not
run. `prtriage` reads `reviewers` and `triage.marker` and nothing else.
A registry that declares policy no consumer here enforces would be two
files' worth of drift in one.

review_markers: This is an auto-generated comment: summarize by coderabbit.ai
reviewers.why: The only reviewer configured on this repository. Its findings-bearing reviews go through the reviews API and are invisible to the queue's `gh pr list --json comments` read, so the walkthrough comment is the comment-shaped proxy for 'a review happened here'. See the $comment above for the measurement and the known limitation.

triage.why: A heading, matched at the start of a line, so that quoting it inside prose does not read as a disposition. Recording the disposition on the PR is what makes the Definition of Done's Review item checkable by someone other than its author — including when there was nothing to dispose of, because 'CI green, no findings' is a disposition and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.
